description:
# #830 — Shared WebBridge contracts and BO-first migration

Status: proposed implementation plan.
Date: 2026-10-03.
Source issue: https://github.com/www-zaq-ai/zaq/issues/830.
Implementation branch: `refactor/webbridge`.

## 1. Outcome and delivery scope

Refactor the BO chat integration into the first consumer of a shared web transport contract. BO and the future widget produce the same message and command structs. WebBridge alone translates messages into the existing canonical `Zaq.Engine.Messages.Incoming` struct, maps commands to Engine operations, and translates outbound results using the consumer's trusted delivery contract.

Deliver in four ordered sets:

1. Define and implement the first contracts required by BO.
2. Migrate BO and prove behavioral parity.
3. Extend the contracts and ZAQ-side integration seams required by the widget.
4. Publish the implemented contract and conformance fixtures for the widget developer.

Inbound user-message editing (`message.edit`) is excluded. Outbound assistant updates (`response.message.edit`) remain required for streaming. No second canonical Incoming/Outgoing model, conversation database, authorization engine, or generic protocol/plugin framework is introduced.

Phase 3 delivers ZAQ-side capabilities and executable adapter conformance coverage. Implementing the external widget's LiveView, iframe assets, embed script, and router macro belongs to the widget developer. Actual package installation and production route mounting follow that developer's implementation; this plan must not claim a functioning widget before that integration is tested.

BO's appearance and user-visible feature set are preserved. Existing BO-specific operations such as feedback, previews, conversation deletion/listing, and trace inspection retain their supported domain dispatch paths; this migration does not force them into an unrestricted command bus.

## 2. Planning and execution constraints

- Track implementation tasks in Beadwork with `[830]` title prefixes and the dependencies below.
- Read AGENTS.md and its applicable policy owners. This plan follows `docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md`, `docs/action-reuse.md`, `docs/testing-approach.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md`, and `docs/documentation.md`.
- Preserve regression assertions and document intentional contract migrations. Follow the human UX/UI approval gate before authoring new/substantially rewritten E2E.
- All BO cross-service operations use `%Zaq.Event{}` and `NodeRouter.dispatch/1`. Pure request construction in a BO client is local; invoking WebBridge business/runtime operations directly from LiveView is not.
- Keep new callbacks specific to the web adapter boundary; do not add widget-only requirements to the global Bridge behaviour.

## 3. Infrastructure audit and reuse decisions

| Existing implementation | Evidence and significance | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lib/zaq/channels/web_bridge.ex` | Converts flat BO params, emits `chat:<session_id>` tuples, supports status upserts. No listener ingress or runtime implementation. | Extend into the common web boundary; retain compatibility during migration only. |
| `lib/zaq_web/live/bo/communication/chat_live.ex` | Builds Incoming and Engine routing events itself; supplies BO actor, history, selected agent, content filters and explicit `skip_permissions: true`; owns init/history orchestration and error fallback. | Move transport/routing orchestration to the bridge boundary; retain UI state/rendering in BO. |
| `lib/zaq/channels/api.ex` | `delivery_connection/2` and `upsert_connection/2` already resolve positive `routing_context.channel_config_id` values and reject invalid scoped IDs. `outgoing_to_upsert_request/1` still drops general metadata/delivery context. | Reuse config-scoped delivery and its unscoped BO fallback. Add supported web ingress and opaque delivery-context propagation; do not reimplement connector selection. |
| `lib/zaq/channels/communication_bridge.ex` | Existing routing Event builders and runtime synchronization. | Reuse; extend only where required to preserve BO routing options and per-config context. |
| `lib/zaq/channels/bridge.ex` | Owns incoming hooks, configuration resolution and runtime helpers. | Reuse hooks/runtime helpers; retain Engine-owned admission/finalization. |
| `lib/zaq/channels/supervisor.ex`, `bridge_supervisor.ex` | Static role facade plus dynamic runtime bootstrap/start/stop. There is no current `ChannelSupervisor` module. | Reuse for widget runtime specs and enable/disable/reconfigure. Adapter owns runtime child construction. |
| `lib/zaq/engine/api.ex`, `incoming_message_router.ex` | Routing admits incoming messages through Conversations; Engine exposes `:finalize_incoming` with actor validation. Generic `:conversation` get/messages/create does not enforce ownership. | Preserve admission/finalization. Compose authorized widget operations at Engine's boundary rather than exposing generic conversation reads. |
| `lib/zaq/engine/conversations.ex` | `conversation_for_persistence/3` validates stamped scoped identity against channel type, participant-derived channel user, config, channel and thread. Its unscoped fallback accepts the conversation. | Reuse scope validation and establish trusted widget scope through identity/initialization integration. |
| `lib/zaq/engine/conversations/transcript_history.ex` via `Conversations.list_canonical_messages/3` | Authorized, bounded, sanitized transcript reads validate a persisted Person, transcript freshness/scope and Permissions. Legacy transcripts are denied by the public reader. | Reuse this canonical read/authorization/projection/pagination implementation for compatible widget history. Establish widget conversation-to-transcript binding first; do not assume conversation IDs are transcript IDs. |
| `lib/zaq/engine/history/`, `history_ingress.ex`, canonical transcript/execution-record schemas | Strategy-driven history and separate canonical messages/private execution records already exist. | Discover and reuse the applicable strategy/source facts and storage lifecycle. Do not add a parallel widget history store or expose execution records as public messages. |
| `lib/zaq/engine/people_conversations.ex` | Fixed self-service boundary authenticates a People bearer, checks history permissions, and uses literal-owner queries. | Reuse if the widget identity model is People authentication; do not call it with a fabricated user ID or weaken its bearer contract. |
| `lib/zaq/engine/messages/outgoing.ex` | `from_pipeline_result/2` already copies Incoming routing_context; metadata still merges pipeline results over inbound values. | Preserve the existing routing context and add tests for the remaining trusted delivery-reference propagation/override risks; never expose raw metadata. |
| `lib/zaq/agent/tools/accounts/history.ex` | Person-scoped topic/time recall across conversations, not exact conversation restoration. | Not the widget history operation; reuse underlying scoped Engine APIs rather than invoking an Agent tool from Engine. |
| `lib/zaq/agent/tools/conversations/persist_message_history.ex` | Action persists one message through Engine; it is not initialization or ownership-checked history loading. | Keep existing persistence ownership; do not duplicate this operation. |
| `test/zaq/channels/web_bridge_test.exs`, `test/zaq_web/live/bo/communication/chat_live_test.exs` | Existing transport, streaming, errors, identity/bypass, welcome/history, filtering, feedback and conversation-reuse regression coverage. | Preserve behavior while migrating transport expectations; record exact equivalence in section 10. |
| `test/zaq/engine/conversations/{transcript_history,canonical_history_capture,threading_persistence,legacy_history_cutover}_test.exs`, `test/zaq/channels/api_test.exs` | Existing authorization, canonical history, scoped persistence and connector-delivery coverage. | Extend focused integration cases rather than recreating these test suites. |

Widget history composes the canonical reader with authenticated identity and trusted conversation/config/transcript binding. Any missing initialization operation identified after identity/strategy selection becomes a focused Engine prerequisite. Agent-tool exposure is outside this refactor.

## 4. Proposed contract architecture

Names below are proposed ZAQ-owned API names; freeze them in A1 before implementation.

### 4.1 Modules and responsibilities

| Module / location | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `Zaq.Channels.Web.Message`, `lib/zaq/channels/web/message.ex` | Shared normalized inbound user-message facts and validation. |
| `Zaq.Channels.Web.Command`, `.../command.ex` | Closed set of conversation commands with command-specific parameter validation. |
| `Zaq.Channels.Web.Response`, `.../response.ex` | Shared semantic success/error/status response, independent of a PubSub wire format. |
| `Zaq.Channels.Web.Context`, `.../context.ex` | Explicit trusted execution and delivery context; no browser-derived capabilities. |
| `Zaq.Channels.Web.Delivery`, `.../delivery.ex` | Validated adapter delivery descriptor and semantic-event-to-wire mapping. |
| `Zaq.Channels.WebBridge` | Ingress normalization to Incoming, command delegation, response translation and delivery; public ingress `from_listener/3`. |
| `ZaqWeb.Chat.BridgeClient`, `lib/zaq_web/chat/bridge_client.ex` | BO-local payload/context construction and Channels Event dispatch; no Incoming construction or Engine execution. |
| `Zaq.Channels.Api` | Fixed web-ingress domain action delegating to WebBridge; existing delivery actions continue to work. Proposed action name: `:web_ingress`. |
| Engine-owned authorized operation(s) | Resolve identity, verify conversation scope, initialize/resume and read history; reused by transport commands. |

Do not create a module merely to match this table if the responsibility is already cohesively owned; A1 records final names and ownership. Separate structs remain separate files. Existing moduledocs must be updated to match the expanded responsibility before adding functions outside their documented scope.

### 4.2 Shared inbound message

Proposed required fields: `request_id`, `message_id`, `content`, `timestamp`, and a channel reference. Optional transport facts: `conversation_id`, external sender reference, display name, and supported attachments. `mode` is one of the explicitly supported atoms `:sync` or `:async`; adapters parse strings through a closed mapping.

- BO and widget produce this same struct. Their trusted contexts differ.
- `user_id`/sender reference is a transport claim, never a canonical person or authorization grant.
- WebBridge maps validated message facts to Incoming: content, provider `:web`, author reference, message ID, authorized conversation metadata, and canonical routing context.
- Widget config ID belongs in routing context. BO remains the BO channel rather than being assigned a fabricated widget ID.
- Populate existing source/audience/conversation identity facts only according to the selected history strategy. Keep transport, conversation, transcript and execution-record IDs distinct; do not infer canonical history scope from a client-provided ID.
- Selected-agent overrides, filters, supplied BO history, and permission bypass are explicitly typed/allowlisted trusted options; never pass an arbitrary client `pipeline_opts` map through.
- No struct constructor is an authorization mechanism. Validate the public ingress again before side effects.
- Reject unsupported versions/types, blank content, malformed IDs/timestamps and invalid modes with structured errors; preserve BO's current whitespace handling.

### 4.3 Command envelope

Proposed fields: `request_id`, `type`, `conversation_id`, `params`. Initially support `:conversation_init` and `:conversation_history`; add `prompt_context` only with the widget extension and an explicit Engine mapping.

- Initialization with no conversation ID creates/resolves according to the trusted consumer policy. Resume with an ID validates access first.
- BO's current missing-conversation fallback is a named BO policy, not an implicit public-widget fallback.
- Widget `widget.init` translates to the shared initialization command. There is no widget-only command struct.
- Commands return `{:ok, Response.t()}` or `{:error, Response.t()}` synchronously. No fabricated Incoming is used for history/init.
- Unknown commands are rejected. No arbitrary MFA, Event action, module, SQL filter or Repo operation can be selected through command parameters.

### 4.4 Trusted context and adapter delivery descriptor

The authenticated server-side adapter supplies context independently of the message/command. It contains validated actor/authentication context, the consumer identity, supported BO capabilities, and delivery configuration. Missing person identity never grants a bypass. `skip_permissions` means the explicit pipeline permission override already available to BO; it does not mean unrestricted conversation ownership access.

The descriptor supplies the PubSub destination and expected event names, as requested by the consumer:

- A server-resolved topic, derived from validated session/widget/conversation scope.
- A closed semantic-event-to-external-name map.
- A bounded wire envelope option: shared response map, or a fixed tagged response envelope for BO. Avoid arbitrary code/template evaluation.
- Required response correlation fields and the consumer's supported event set.
- A trusted adapter/configuration reference and protocol version, resolved from server configuration rather than a browser-chosen module.

WebBridge performs the actual mapping/broadcast. The adapter defines expectations; it does not receive Incoming/Outgoing internals to reimplement pipeline translation. Adapter runtime specs and transport construction remain adapter-owned.

Before a new conversation exists, initialization replies synchronously. The server then resolves the conversation topic; the client subscribes before submitting `message.create`. This avoids publishing the only initialization result to a topic the client cannot yet know.

BO may retain `chat:<session_id>`; widget uses `web_widget:<widget_id>:conversation:<conversation_id>`. No topic is accepted verbatim from browser input. Subscriber authorization belongs at the adapter/Phoenix boundary as well as Engine command authorization.

### 4.5 Internal propagation and response semantics

- Carry only a namespaced, serializable delivery reference/snapshot across Incoming/Outgoing and role hops. No socket, PID, function closure, bearer credential, or arbitrary runtime module goes into persisted message metadata.
- Prefer reconstructible server configuration plus scoped IDs over copying the full Context. Retain the producer's actor on `%Zaq.Event.actor`; never serialize it into public responses.
- Channels may forward the opaque web context without inspecting its widget keys; WebBridge is its interpreter. Changes to shared status conversion must preserve all existing providers.
- Reuse Outgoing.routing_context and Channels' existing config-scoped connection resolution. Preserve Engine admission/finalization bindings internally; finalization tokens and private execution-record data must never become public response fields.
- `Response` carries protocol version, request ID, semantic type, conversation/message correlation, and an allowlisted payload. BO needs sources, confidence, persistence IDs, error information, and authorized message-info data. Widget projection excludes private execution traces, credentials and internal pipeline metadata; visible steps are sanitized status/tool summaries.
- Streaming updates carry full current assistant content initially, matching BO's existing replacement behavior even where the legacy intent is called `stream_delta`. Document this clearly; do not silently switch to append-only token deltas.
- Persisted database message IDs and transport/request message IDs are distinct. Completion may supply the persisted ID used by feedback/history.
- Define one terminal-response owner. The existing ChatLive error fallback must migrate with regression coverage; do not broadcast both a pipeline terminal response and a second fallback terminal response.
- PubSub is live best-effort delivery, not durable replay. Restore from authorized history after reconnect. Do not automatically retry an uncertain accepted message or claim durable exactly-once processing.

### 4.6 Proposed widget event mapping

| Shared operation/event | Widget wire name / behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Initialization command | `widget.init` inbound; `response.widget.initialized` synchronous response containing resolved conversation ID |
| Actual new conversation creation | `response.conversation.created`; return as an initialization result notification when no topic subscription yet exists; do not rely on an early PubSub broadcast |
| History command | `conversation.history.request` inbound; `response.conversation.history` synchronous response |
| Message | `message.create` inbound; sync acceptance for async execution, correlated outbound events thereafter |
| Typing | `response.typing` with explicit active/inactive state |
| Assistant started | `response.message.create` with stable transport message ID |
| Assistant content update | `response.message.edit`, full-content replacement |
| Visible activity | `response.message.step`, sanitized step ID, message ID, kind, state and label |
| Success | `response.message.complete`, final content and safe persisted references |
| Execution failure | `response.message.failed`, correlated safe error |
| Validation/protocol failure | `response.error`, structured code/message/request ID |

Freeze the precise created-notification representation and sync-message behavior in C1. An async receipt acknowledges accepted work, not successful execution. A synchronous message returns the terminal response; it must not also emit a duplicate terminal response to the same consumer. No unbounded in-memory replay/deduplication store is required by v1.

## 5. Task graph and deliverables

Create one issue per task below, using the label as its title prefix, plus an umbrella `[830] WebBridge contracts refactor`. Gate issues stay open until their required evidence/approval is recorded.

Primary dependency chain (deliberately linear to make the BO-first gate unambiguous):

`A0 → A1 → A2 → A3 → B1 → B2 → B3 → B4 → C1 → C2 → C3 → C4 → D1 → D2 → V1`

Phases A/B may land separately from C/D. Do not migrate BO and add widget behavior in the same unreviewed change. C1 can be discussed earlier, but widget implementation remains blocked on B4. If splitting tasks further, preserve these dependencies and justify any necessary diamond.

Every task includes immediate test-first coverage unless it is purely a decision/documentation gate. Shared mocking rule: real internal boundaries and isolated SQL Sandbox/PubSub; fake only external LLM/widget transport behind its actual production interface. No new public test-only hooks or global configuration mutation. Runtime dependencies resolve through the existing opts/Event carrier and `Zaq.Config` at the public boundary.



## 10. Existing-test contract migration and regression requirements

Document the following intentional transport/boundary changes while preserving user-facing and history guarantees. Never weaken assertions, skip tests or change expected outcomes to hide regressions; new/substantially rewritten E2E requires B3 approval.

| Existing assertion/scenario | Proposed contract | Regression requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WebBridge accepts flat BO maps and defaults the channel to `bo`. | Shared Message validation plus trusted BO context; temporary compatibility until B4. | Preserve BO channel selection and input validation while retiring the flat-map API. |
| WebBridge sends `{:pipeline_result, ...}` / `{:status_update, ...}`. | Adapter-declared normalized response envelope, same status/content/final/error meaning. | Migrate wire assertions with equivalent rendering and correlation tests. |
| ChatLive tests inspect direct Engine routing dispatch from the LiveView. | LiveView dispatches shared ingress to Channels; Engine receives equivalent canonical request/actor/options. | Retain downstream actor, routing, bypass and admission/finalization assertions. |
| ChatLive tests stub direct conversation get/create/messages. | Same visible behavior via Command and supported role dispatch. | Preserve welcome, fallback, persistence and history outcomes. |
| Tests accept matching nil request IDs or malformed legacy status intent. | New ingress requires valid correlation; any legacy tolerance is confined to compatibility handling. | Present exact tests before narrowing accepted behavior; do not quietly delete them as obsolete. |
| Error fallback tests rely on direct LiveView PID messages. | Bridge-owned normalized failure delivery with the same rendered error and no duplicate final bubble. | Preserve fallback/error regression assertions across the transport change. |
| Canonical history and config-scoped delivery already have dedicated tests. | Web ingress composes those existing contracts. | Preserve authorization denial, legacy rejection, pagination, scoped persistence and per-config destination isolation. |

Relevant tests include `web_bridge_test.exs` send/upsert expectations, and ChatLive cases for matching request IDs, stream replacement, nil correlation, dispatch-error Outgoing, persistence failures, missing-conversation fallback and explicit BO bypass.

## 11. Decisions to resolve before the relevant phase

### Before A1/A2

1. Freeze the public contract names and signatures: ZAQ-owned shared structs, fixed Channels ingress action, synchronous init/history, explicit trusted BO context and adapter-supplied delivery descriptor.
2. Freeze the smallest BO response/history projection that preserves existing sources, ratings, message-info/trace controls and persistence references. Do not dump raw Outgoing metadata into a universal response.
3. Confirm how welcome-message initialization remains single-owned and how legacy missing-conversation fallback is represented. Preserve BO behavior unless a separate change is approved.

### Before C2–C4

4. **Widget identity:** People bearer, another verified identity mapping, or anonymous sessions? Issue #830's arbitrary `user_id` is not an authentication contract. Do not invent anonymous grants. This blocks public authorization implementation, not BO refactoring.
5. **Widget init/resume scope:** define the binding among principal, widget/config ID, channel selector, conversation and canonical transcript, including the applicable existing history strategy and permission resource. Do not assume a web conversation automatically has a public-readable canonical transcript. Default recommendation: public resume of a deleted/unknown conversation fails rather than silently changing identity.
6. **Prompt context:** exact Engine input, provenance, size/lifetime and persistence policy. It must remain untrusted context and cannot override system policy, routing authority or actor permissions. Do not merely append it as a privileged system message.
7. **Sync message mode:** define timeout and terminal-return behavior separately from async acceptance. An uncertain timeout must not cause automatic duplicate execution.
8. **History bounds:** adapt the existing canonical reader's cursor/upper-bound/limit contract to the widget wire format; preserve ordering and safe projection. Keep BO restoration behavior intact and specify legacy/unbound-conversation behavior without using an unauthorized fallback.
9. **External dependency shape:** agree the host adapter/construction hook so both clients produce identical ZAQ structs without a cyclic ZAQ↔widget dependency.
10. **Domain/style policy:** define allowed-domain matching, empty lists, localhost and wildcard behavior; distinguish iframe embedding, WebSocket origin and conversation authorization. Resolve `stylesheet_url` against ZAQ's locally served product-asset policy rather than assuming arbitrary remote stylesheet loading is allowed.
11. **Creation notification:** freeze how `response.conversation.created` is represented in the synchronous initialization exchange before the conversation topic is subscribed.

These are explicit prerequisite decisions, not permission to implement guessed behavior. Record answers in the owning issues and contract documentation when resolved.

## 12. Completion checklist

- [ ] BO and widget fixture construct the same Message/Command structs.
- [ ] WebBridge is the sole web-input → canonical Incoming translator.
- [ ] BO sends through Channels/NodeRouter and retains explicit trusted capabilities.
- [ ] Commands delegate to Engine; widget conversation access is authorized before reads/writes.
- [ ] Adapter-supplied topic/event expectations drive bridge delivery without browser-controlled destinations.
- [ ] Status and final paths preserve correlation/context across role boundaries.
- [ ] Existing config-scoped delivery, canonical reader permission/pagination, scoped persistence and Engine admission/finalization are reused and regression-tested.
- [ ] BO parity, failure behavior and adjacent features are verified; approved legacy paths are removed.
- [ ] Widget sync/async event and runtime contracts pass conformance tests without duplicating infrastructure.
- [ ] Outbound streaming edits are supported; inbound user-message editing is excluded.
- [ ] Final contract docs/examples match implementation and widget developer responsibilities are explicit.
- [ ] Approval, test, coverage and final validation gates are recorded in Beadwork before final handoff/merge approval.


## Authorization
The user approved this plan and requested Beadwork issue creation. Implementation has not started. BO UX/E2E approval remains outstanding; C1 product/security decisions remain prerequisites.
